prose.summary: Mansha cannot confirm whether the aluminium window frames qualify for the preferential rate under the India-UAE CEPA because the required information is missing. To complete the origin check, please provide a bill of materials, a declaration, and the shipment value in AED. The duty saving cannot be estimated without the shipment value.
prose.classification: The product is classified under tariff line 76101000, which covers doors, windows and their frames and thresholds for doors (aluminium). Mansha's confidence in this classification is high, but you should confirm the code with Indian customs or a customs broker before shipping.
prose.duty: Under the India-UAE CEPA, the normal (MFN) rate is 10% and the CEPA rate is 0%. The duty saving cannot be estimated without the shipment value.
prose.origin: The rule of origin for this product is change in tariff subheading (CTSH) plus 45% value addition (VA). CTSH requires that each non-originating input is classified in a different 6-digit subheading than the final product, and VA requires that at least 45% of the product's price does not come from non-originating materials. The origin check cannot be performed yet because the required information is missing, specifically a bill of materials and a declaration. No checks were performed to verify if these conditions are met.

notes.text: Simple operations like packing, loading, or minor assembly, even when combined, never make a product originating under the CEPA rules. Additionally, cumulation is bilateral, so originating materials from India used in production in the UAE can be counted as originating, but the final manufacturing step in the UAE must still go beyond minimal operations.

The Social Welfare Surcharge (SWS) is still charged on the reduced Basic Customs Duty, and anti-dumping or safeguard duties still apply without exemption. The certificate fee ranges from AED 10 to AED 200, depending on the invoice value in AED.
Mansha interprets '+' in the rule as 'and' (both tests must pass). The agreement does not define '+', so this is an interpretation.
No usable shipment value was provided, so only rates are given.
The CEPA rate reduces Basic Customs Duty (BCD) only. IGST, GST compensation cess, SWS and any anti-dumping or safeguard duty still apply.
The CEPA rate applies only if the product qualifies under the rules of origin and a valid certificate of origin is presented.

'Direct labour cost' and 'direct overhead cost' are not defined in the agreement. The agreement does not say whether the build-down and build-up methods use the same threshold, apart from the 5-point Ex-Works adjustment.
Operations listed in Art. 3.5.1 (a) to (q), alone or combined, never make a product originating, whatever the product-specific rule says.

Cumulation is bilateral only: originating materials from India used in production in the UAE may be counted as originating. The last production process in the UAE must still go beyond the minimal operations.
The agreement says box 8, but India's origin rules and certificate form say box 9; India's form governs entry into India.
UAE law sets a shorter 3-year minimum; the CEPA's 5 years governs CEPA claims.

No official page read names the Ministry of Foreign Trade as the issuer of the India CEPA certificate specifically: its service page covers preferential certificates in general, and the India-specific page is still on moet.gov.ae.

A producer in a free zone is likely not eligible for Factory Registration, because it requires a factory outside a free zone, and registration is needed before applying for the certificate of origin for India. Confirm with the Ministry of Economy and Tourism.

Electronic certificates are reportedly accepted and uploaded to India's e-Sanchit system, but this is seen only in secondary sources (CBIC Instruction 28/2022 read through LiveLaw, taxmann), not the official text.
The Social Welfare Surcharge (SWS) is charged on the reduced BCD (no CEPA-specific text found). Anti-dumping and safeguard duties still apply (no exemption found).
The fee range is AED 10 to AED 200 because no shipment value was provided; the exact fee depends on the invoice value in AED.
